title: script-standards-detail.md requires every ACTION to pair with a same-text log_warn, but write_summary then promotes every later OK row to WARN (undocumented) against D-TS12, so the lib and the config writer pair ACTIONs with log_error or different text instead
observation: scripts/aitools-lib.sh write_summary (:860-866 on origin/main 8a9dcb5): 'Auto-promote OK to WARN when warnings have been logged' (`if [ "$cat" = "OK" ] && [ "${WARNINGS:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then cat="WARN"`); scripts/aitools-lib.ps1 Write-Summary (:752-757) the same. reference/script-standards-detail.md 'Severity decision guide' (:239-243): '`log_warn` + `write_summary ACTION` -- user action required; always pair ACTION with a log_warn carrying the same instruction', and 'ACTION items' repeats it; neither section mentions the promotion. scripts/setup-user-config.sh:367-370 works around it by hand: 'It must stay after the config row: write_summary promotes an OK row to WARN once a warning is counted'. S3-MF-Audit (A-5, A-10) found 7 ACTION sites per language in the lib wrappers that follow a log_error or a log_warn with different text, e.g. aitools-lib.sh:290-292 `log_error "dotprofile: resolver aitools-profile not found next to aitools-lib.sh"` + ACTION `see deploy.log -- the dotprofile could not be resolved`; the lib's comment (:327-329) says resolver warnings stay detail lines so 'a successful step stays OK, D-TS12'. setup-user-config.sh:216-222 adds ERROR + ACTION rows with no log line carrying the instruction.
expected: reference/script-standards-detail.md 'Severity decision guide' and 'ACTION items' (always pair ACTION with a log_warn carrying the same instruction) conflict with D-TS12 (reference/tool-support-decision-tree.md:64: 'a step that succeeds without errors reports OK, never downgraded to WARN by its own result') once write_summary auto-promotes (aitools-lib.sh:860-866). No spec exists for: how an ACTION pairs with an ERROR, or which log level carries an advisory ACTION's text.
impact: A script that follows the guide (log_warn + ACTION before its own OK row) reports WARN for a tool that is fine, so the summary panel overstates problems; each script author rediscovers the trap (S3-M3-ConfigKey and its reviewer did on PR #86).
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-ConfigKey-report.md:87 and S3-M3-ConfigKey-Review-pr86-batch4.md:115 (PR #86 batch 4). Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-lib.sh:855-866, scripts/aitools-lib.ps1:752-760, reference/script-standards-detail.md:239-265 ('Severity decision guide', 'Summary coverage rule', 'ACTION items'), scripts/setup-user-config.sh:363-376. Audited #1-#145: #142 (duplicate ERROR rows) is a different summary defect. A draft doc edit exists (S3-M3-Docs approval page row 15, script-standards-detail.md.edit.txt). Extended 2026-10-22 with S3-MF-Audit-findings.md section 8 (PR #104, branch docs/mf-audit) marker I-2 ('Same root as the S3-M3-ConfigKey-Review INCIDENT on auto-promote'), merged here instead of a second entry; re-verified aitools-lib.sh:288-294 and :322-332, reference/tool-support-decision-tree.md:64.
suggestedResolution: Decide the pairing rule first (protected script-standards-detail.md), then align the code sites (audit FIX-3 and the lib sites of A-5). Options: (A) document the promotion and require the tool's own row before an advisory log_warn + ACTION (the S3-M3-Docs draft, row 15); (B) an ACTION that accompanies an ERROR pairs with its log_error, and an advisory ACTION pairs with a `log` (info) line carrying the same text, so nothing is promoted (audit suggestion); (C) exempt ACTION-paired warnings from promotion in the lib (an advisory-warning counter, bash and PS1). B matches D-TS12 and today's lib behaviour.

title: No logging contract or script-standards exemption exists for library-style tools (the profile resolver: data on stdout, diagnostics returned as warn/error lines, no exit footer or summary rows), so each caller routes the returned warnings on its own
observation: scripts/aitools-profile.sh returns diagnostics instead of logging them at level: cmd_user_repo_path prints its warnings as 'warning: ...' lines on stderr and its result on stdout (:770-781 on origin/main 8a9dcb5); it defines log() to stderr before logging_init (:71-79). Callers route them by hand: scripts/setup-user-config.sh derive_warn (:165 onward) sorts each returned warning into 'handled', 'advisory' and 'real' with its own patterns; aitools-lib.sh tool_exception_record logs returned warn lines as detail (:432). reference/logging.md has sections 1-6 (Location, Path separators, Granularity, Rotation, Format, Setup-vs-check) and no section for library-style tools; the script-standards-detail.md exemptions table has no resolver row. Before ConfigKey (PR #86 batch 4) setup-user-config turned every returned warning into a WARN row (S3-M3-Resolver-Review M-finding); that code is fixed, the contract is still unwritten. The resolver's contract lives only in its own header (aitools-profile.sh:39-43: 'Logging contract (library-style tool): every warning and error is returned as a warn / error line ... the caller logs each at its level and owns the summary rows and counters'); reference/script-standards-detail.md 'Exemptions table' (:1156) has no such category. Four bash internal-error paths print to stderr and exit 2 with no log_detail (e.g. aitools-profile.sh:167 `printf 'aitools-profile: internal error reading %s ...' >&2; exit 2`; also :181, :194, :207), so deploy.log has them only when the caller copies stderr (S3-MF-Audit A-6).
expected: No spec exists for: how a tool that returns diagnostics (rather than logging them) reports them, and which returned warnings a caller must count. .claude/rules/script-standards.md 'Error and warning tracking requirement' assumes every script logs and counts its own warnings.
impact: Every new consumer of the resolver (deploy-harness, tool setup scripts in M2) must invent its own warning routing; a wrong choice either downgrades the summary row on every run (the pre-fix setup-user-config behaviour) or hides a real problem at info level.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-Register-keydesign.md:411 (design j finding 1), S3-M3-Resolver-report.md:123 and :125, S3-M3-Resolver-Review-pr86-batch2.md:166. Merged into one entry: the advisory-vs-row-level marker is the same missing contract (its code instance was fixed in setup-user-config.sh:160-185). Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-profile.sh:71-79 and :768-780, scripts/setup-user-config.sh:160-185, grep of reference/logging.md headings and reference/script-standards-detail.md. A draft logging.md section 7 'Library-style tools' exists (S3-M3-Docs approval page row 16). Extended 2026-10-22 with S3-MF-Audit-findings.md section 8 (PR #104, branch docs/mf-audit) marker I-3 (no exemption category), merged here; re-verified aitools-profile.sh:36-45 and :165-168 and the script-standards-detail.md 'Exemptions table' heading.
suggestedResolution: Approve the S3-M3-Docs draft of reference/logging.md section 7 (protected), extended with the advisory/row-level split that setup-user-config.sh derive_warn already implements; add the resolver to the script-standards-detail.md exemptions table. Optional: the resolver tags each warning with its class so callers stop pattern-matching message text. The exemptions-table row should state: no exit footer, no summary rows, diagnostics returned, raw stderr allowed. Also add log_detail before each of the four bash `printf ... >&2; exit 2` paths (audit FIX-6).
correctiveAction: Code instance fixed: setup-user-config.sh derive_warn routes advisory warnings to info + one ACTION (PR #86 batch 4).

title: The naming and scope contract for shared-library results (AITLIB_ globals, dot-sourced PowerShell scope, function names a caller also defines) exists only as a code comment in aitools-lib.sh, and the installers already shadow two lib functions
observation: scripts/aitools-lib.sh:125-134 (origin/main 8a9dcb5): 'Result-global contract (PR #80 review3 B1/M1): every result global carries the AITLIB_ prefix and every private helper the _aitlib_ prefix, so they cannot collide with a caller's own variables'. grep -i 'AITLIB|dot-sourc|result global|prefix' over reference/script-standards-detail.md, reference/cross-platform-detail.md and .claude/rules/script-standards.md: no hits. Shadowing: aitools-lib.sh:569 defines relay_child_log and scripts/aitools-install.sh:153 defines its own; aitools-lib.ps1:449 defines Write-JsonlRecord and scripts/aitools-install.ps1:65 defines its own (after dot-sourcing the lib, so the caller's copy wins).
expected: Incident #9 already records 'No spec exists for: when and how entry points may override library functions' for scripts/aitools-install.sh/.ps1; the installer shadowing below is a current instance of that gap. No spec exists for: naming of shared-library result variables, the scope of a dot-sourced PowerShell library, or what a caller's definition of a lib function name means. .claude/rules/script-standards.md 'Required logging helpers' says 'Do not define inline copies' for logging helpers only.
impact: The PR #80 collisions (review3 B1/M1: lib results overwrote callers' USER_REPO_PATH) can recur in any new lib section, since the rule lives where only readers of that block see it; a lib fix to relay_child_log or Write-JsonlRecord silently does not reach the installers that shadow them.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-LibFix-report.md:129 (repeating the Review3 marker on PR #80) and S3-M3-LibKey-report.md:95. Merged: same missing contract. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-lib.sh:120-150, grep for relay_child_log / Write-JsonlRecord / jsonl_record definitions in the lib and installers, grep of the three spec files. The Review3 full report is not in the repo (PR #82 points to it); its other markers are unknown. Audited #1-#145: #9 (entry point logging override pattern) covers the override half and is named in expected; this entry adds the result-naming/scope contract and the two live shadowed functions.
suggestedResolution: Add a 'Library contract' paragraph to reference/script-standards-detail.md 'Shared library' (protected): AITLIB_/_aitlib_ and $script:AitLib* prefixes, assignment only inside functions, callers copy results right after the call, and callers never redefine a lib function (or must name the override, as entry-point logging does). Then remove or rename the installers' relay_child_log / Write-JsonlRecord copies, or record them as deliberate overrides.

title: The two JSON engines write the same number differently (aitools-json.pl keeps the source text such as 0.10; aitools-json.ps1 writes 0.1), so bash and PowerShell writers of one shared file produce different bytes
observation: scripts/aitools-json.pl:68-70 (origin/main 8a9dcb5): 'Numbers keep their source lexeme byte for byte' (`sub numnorm { return $_[0] }`). scripts/aitools-json.ps1 parses with `ConvertFrom-Json` (:35) into a Double and writes with ConvertTo-NodeJson (:170-174), which loses the source lexeme: the PR #102 reviewer's pwsh 7.6.3 probe rewrote 0.10 as 0.1 and 1e2 as 100.0 (ConvertTo-JText :66-69, the `get` output, formats doubles the same way). The S3-M3-JsonRename reviewer verified the difference with a round trip on the base aitools-json.ps1 (PR #86 comment); not re-run here.
expected: .claude/rules/cross-platform.md 'Platform targeting principle' (paired scripts behave the same); the resolver and profile.json are written by both engines (commander decision: dotprofile writes auto-commit and push, N-Q2).
impact: A profile.json value with trailing zeros changes bytes when a Windows machine rewrites it, so the dotprofile gets diff-only commits that flip between machines; byte-level comparisons between bash and PS1 test outputs fail.
discoveryContext: Marker in S3-M3-JsonRename-report.md:69 (from its reviewer, PR #86 re-key batch 1). Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5 by reading scripts/aitools-json.pl:60-72 and scripts/aitools-json.ps1:14-35 and :170-174; round trip probe by the PR #102 reviewer (S3-MF-Incidents-Review), not by the author. Audited #1-#145: no match.
suggestedResolution: Keep the source lexeme in the PS1 engine too (parse numbers into a wrapper that carries the original text, as perl does), and add a parity case with 0.10 and a 17-digit value to tests/profile/test-profile.sh for both engines.

title: No rule says each pushed batch of a stacked PR keeps CI green or declares a deliberately red CI, so a batch landed with macOS and Linux CI red and an ordinary commit message
observation: Commit b70fc64 'Key machine profiles by machine id in the native resolver (re-key batch 2)' (2026-10-22) was pushed to the stacked re-key PR #86 with the macos and linux CI jobs red, and its message did not mention a CI failure (S3-M3-Resolver-Review-pr86-batch2.md finding M1, marker :165). grep -i 'CI green|keeps CI|red CI' over .claude, reference and shared: no hits.
expected: No spec exists for: CI status of intermediate pushed batches on a stacked PR. Nearest: /delegate D-DEL4 shipping terms (run the repo's checks before push) and #144 (merge gating on review verdicts).
impact: A red batch in a stack hides whether later batches broke CI or inherited the failure, and reviewers of the next batch start from an unknown baseline; reviewers and the commander learn it only from the CI page.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-Resolver-Review-pr86-batch2.md:165 and S3-M3-Resolver-report.md:124. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified: `git log -1 b70fc64`, grep of .claude, reference and shared. The CI run state itself was not re-checked (from the reviewer).
frameworks: Trunk-based development 'keep the build green': every pushed change passes CI, or the push says why not (a declared, tracked red build).
suggestedResolution: Add to /delegate D-DEL4 shipping terms and reference/pre-push-checklist.md: each pushed batch keeps CI green; a deliberately red batch says so in its commit message and PR body with the reason and the batch that turns it green. Optional detection: reviewers check `gh pr checks` per batch.

title: The lib's resolver runner trusts an exit code only with a 'via' result line, which register and migrate never print, and the output-validation rule it implements is written nowhere outside the lib
observation: scripts/aitools-lib.sh _aitlib_profile_run (:154-159, :216-225 on origin/main 8a9dcb5): 'every resolver command prints a "via" line on 0 (found) and 1 (none). Exit 0 or 1 without one ... is rewritten to 2'. scripts/aitools-profile.sh emits `put via` only in user-repo-path (:783), resolve (:872), exception-get (:907), exception-set (:1040) and the profile command (:1147); cmd_register (:1219) and cmd_migrate (:1443) print none. scripts/aitools:196-201 therefore keeps its own runner: 'Not the lib runner ... register and migrate print no "via" line'. No lib wrapper calls register or migrate today (grep 'register|migrate' in scripts/aitools-lib.sh: comments only, :138, :319, :367), so the mismatch is latent. reference/script-standards-detail.md 'External command error handling' says nothing about validating a child's output before trusting its exit code; the resolver's 'not found' exit 1 equals a set -e death and pwsh's own failure code (S3-M3-LibFix-Review M1).
expected: The lib's own header contract (aitools-lib.sh:154) claims every resolver command prints a via line; .claude/rules/script-standards.md 'External command error handling' (check exit codes, distinguish failure modes). No spec exists for: validating a child tool's result lines before trusting its exit code.
impact: The first lib wrapper for register or migrate (deploy-harness or M2 tool scripts) reports every successful registration as a resolver error; meanwhile user init carries a second runner that can drift from the lib's.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-UserInit-report.md:96 (owner: lib) and S3-M3-LibFix-Review-pr80.md:199 (no rule). Merged: the rule the lib implements and the case where it misfires. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-lib.sh:136-225, grep `put via` in scripts/aitools-profile.sh, scripts/aitools:196-205. Parallel mission S3-MF-Adopt owns scripts/aitools-lib.* now; this entry does not assume its outcome.
suggestedResolution: Accept a `result` line as well as `via` in _aitlib_profile_run / Invoke-AitLibProfile (the UserInit report's fix), then let user init use the lib runner. Document the rule in reference/script-standards-detail.md 'External command error handling' (protected): a wrapper trusts a child's exit code only together with the child's result lines, and a child whose failure codes collide with shell/runtime codes must print result lines.

title: The isolated-HOME rule for test and probe runs does not cover the working directory, so a relative path from a fixture's config.json wrote into the main checkout
observation: S3-M3-UserInit-Review-pr86-batch5.md:125: 'A relative path in a fixture's config.json (or any relative path a script takes from config) writes into the agent's cwd, here the main checkout. Probe and test scripts should cd into scratch first.' The mission packet section 5 says 'isolated HOME under your worktree scratch (#86)'; shared/skills/delegate/SKILL.md (origin/main 8a9dcb5) mentions isolated HOME at :184 and :212-213 and has no cwd or working-directory instruction (grep -i 'cwd|working directory': no hits). The relative-repos-path regression itself was fixed in PR #89. Temp files leak the same way: macOS `mktemp` without a template prefers _CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR over TMPDIR (man mktemp), so `TMPDIR=<scratch>/ mktemp`, `mktemp -d` and `mktemp -t x` all wrote to /var/folders/.../T (S3-MF-Incidents probe-final.sh, reproduced by the PR #102 reviewer; marker from PR #116).
expected: Mission packet section 5 and incident #86/#140: test and probe runs must not touch the real user state or the main checkout. No spec exists for: the working directory of isolated test runs.
impact: A delegate following the isolated-HOME rule exactly can still write fixture output into the main checkout (or any directory it was launched from), where it is mistaken for real work, harvested, or committed by another agent.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-UserInit-report.md:98 and S3-M3-UserInit-Review-pr86-batch5.md:125. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: grep of shared/skills/delegate/SKILL.md for HOME and cwd. The reviewer's write into the main checkout was not re-run. Related #140 (worktree isolation refuses HOME overrides), #86.
suggestedResolution: Add one line to /delegate 'Environment limits' and the dotprofile delegation.md (protected): isolated runs set HOME and cd into the scratch directory first (or pass absolute paths only), and probes check that no file appeared outside scratch (`git status` of the launch directory before/after). For temp files, isolated runs pass an explicit directory (`mktemp -p "$SCRATCH"` or a full template) instead of relying on TMPDIR.

title: cross-platform-detail.md omits three traps that broke M3 code or tests: PowerShell variable names ignore case, success-stream output from in-process child scripts becomes a function's return value, and .ps1 files are checked out with CRLF
observation: (1) S3-M3-Resolver-report.md:126: '`foreach ($e in $E)` silently overwrote the collection in Invoke-Migrate (found by the parity tests, fixed)'. (2) S3-M3-UserInit-Review-pr86-batch5.md:126 (m1): a PowerShell function that returns an exit code and runs a child script in-process without discarding its output stream returns that output, so `exit (Fn)` exits 0. (3) .gitattributes:2 `*.ps1 text eol=crlf`; tests/profile/test-user-init.sh:328-329 adds `\r?` before `$` because line-anchored perl patterns miss CRLF lines. reference/cross-platform-detail.md (origin/main 8a9dcb5) has sections for pipeline encoding, clipboard, working directory, Refresh-Path, Git Bash PATH shadowing and Strawberry Perl text mode, and none for these three.
expected: .claude/rules/cross-platform.md 'Windows platform gotchas' points to reference/cross-platform-detail.md for platform traps. No spec exists for: these three.
impact: Each trap fails silently (a clobbered variable, a wrong exit code, a test that matches nothing and passes); the next PowerShell or test author rediscovers them.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-Resolver-report.md:126, S3-M3-UserInit-report.md:99 and :100, S3-M3-UserInit-Review-pr86-batch5.md:126. Merged: all three are missing gotcha entries in the same file with the same fix. Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: cat .gitattributes, read tests/profile/test-user-init.sh:325-337, grep of reference/cross-platform-detail.md headings. Traps (1) and (2) are cited from the reports (code instances fixed), not reproduced.
suggestedResolution: Add three short gotcha sections to reference/cross-platform-detail.md and one-line pointers in .claude/rules/cross-platform.md 'Windows platform gotchas' (protected): distinct variable names that differ by more than case; `$null = & child.ps1` or `| Out-Null` inside functions whose return value is used; `\r?$` (or strip CR) in line-anchored patterns over .ps1 files.
correctiveAction: Instances fixed in PR #86 (Invoke-Migrate variable rename; user init output handling; test-user-init.sh CRLF-tolerant patterns).

title: profile.json scaffolded by the resolver (register --create, user init on a dotprofile without one) carries only meta.schemaRevision, no meta.intent
observation: scripts/aitools-profile.sh:1242 (origin/main 8a9dcb5) writes `edit_set string "2.2" meta schemaRevision` for a new profile.json; scripts/aitools-profile.ps1:1085 adds only schemaRevision to meta. grep 'intent' in aitools-profile.sh finds only a header comment (:23). The approved row-4 intent text for profile.json exists as a draft (S3-M3-Docs approval page open question 3, R23, profile.json.edit.txt).
expected: No spec exists for: an intent statement in profile.json. The R23 draft (S3-M3-Docs approval page open question 3, profile.json.edit.txt) proposes one; registries carry meta.intent (registries/incidents.json meta.intent). Related #104 (intent statements missing elsewhere).

title: When profile.json already had uncommitted changes, tool_exception_record tells the user to 'run git push' although the resolver committed nothing
observation: scripts/aitools-profile.sh commit_profile (:960-970 on origin/main 8a9dcb5): with profile.json dirty before the write, exception-set writes the file but does not commit it and warns 'profile.json had uncommitted changes before this write -- not committed automatically; review and commit profile.json in $dir by hand'. scripts/aitools-lib.sh tool_exception_record (:439-447) picks the first warn line matching /commit|push|git repository/, logs 'tool exception for $slug saved but not pushed (...)' and adds ACTION 'run git push in <dotprofile>'; scripts/aitools-lib.ps1 (:371-376) does the same.
expected: reference/script-standards-detail.md 'Severity decision guide' (an ACTION is the instruction the user must follow); the resolver's own warning says to review and commit by hand.
impact: The user runs `git push` as told, pushes nothing (or pushes unrelated commits), and the tool exception stays uncommitted on this machine only, so the other machines never see the decision.
discoveryContext: Markers in S3-M3-Docs-Check-findings.md:160 and S3-M3-Docs-approval-page.md:103 (finding F18). Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22. Verified on origin/main 8a9dcb5: read scripts/aitools-lib.sh:405-478, scripts/aitools-lib.ps1:360-380, scripts/aitools-profile.sh:947-972. The marker's second half (wrapper headers describe exit 3 as 'matched by hostname only or not at all') was not verified against the resolver's refusal cases and is not part of this entry. title: No spec says whether a consumer counts its own error again after a lib wrapper already logged the resolver failure (log_error + ERROR row), and the B8 consumers disagree

impact: One resolver failure yields a different error count and different row wording per consumer, so the run's error total and exit status depend on which consumers ran; the cursor row uses the governed word 'skipped' for a failure.
discoveryContext: Marker I-4 in S3-MF-Audit-findings.md section 8 (PR #104, branch docs/mf-audit) (related finding A-23). title: Dotprofile auto-push runs a bare `git push`, which pushes the current branch (not necessarily main) and also publishes every earlier unpushed local commit, and no spec says either is intended
observation: dotprofile_commit_push (PR #103 head 945deb5, aitools-lib.sh:1086) and the resolver's commit_profile push (aitools-profile.sh:993) both run `git -C "$dir" push` with no remote or refspec, after a pathspec commit of one file (aitools-lib.sh:1016-1017, :1077). With git's default push.default=simple that pushes the checked-out branch to its upstream, including any commits already on it that were never pushed. Neither checks the branch name or counts the commits ahead of the upstream. PowerShell twins on 945deb5: aitools-lib.ps1:999 and aitools-profile.ps1:831 (`& git -C $dir push`). On origin/main 8a9dcb5 (the PR is still open): the resolver's bare push is at aitools-profile.sh:993.
expected: .claude/rules/managed-file-deployment.md :35 says the adopt target is 'committed and pushed to its main automatically (N-Q2)'. No spec exists for: pushing when the dotprofile is on another branch, or when it already has unpushed local commits.
impact: A dotprofile checked out on a work branch gets that branch pushed (main never receives the change, so other machines do not see it), and a local commit the user kept back on purpose is published by an unrelated adopt or tool-exception write.
discoveryContext: Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22, from the final marker batch relayed by S3-M3Finish. Marker from PR #103. Verified on 945deb5: aitools-lib.sh:1005-1100, aitools-profile.sh:960-1000; spec grep of .claude/rules/managed-file-deployment.md and reference/user-repo.md for 'push'. Audited #1-#164: #156 (wrong ACTION when nothing was committed) is related, not the same.
suggestedResolution: Commander decides the rule, then one helper used by the lib and the resolver. Options: (A) push only when the current branch is main and is at most the new commit ahead of its upstream; otherwise commit only, WARN + ACTION 'push <branch> in <dotprofile>'; (B) always push `HEAD:main` explicitly (refuse on another branch); (C) keep bare `git push` and document that it publishes the current branch and all earlier commits. A is the cautious option. Record it in managed-file-deployment.md and reference/user-repo.md (protected).

title: No spec documents how the JSON engines treat key case (exact-match lookups, refusal of a key that differs only in case); the rule lives only in the aitools-json.pl / .ps1 headers
observation: On PR #108 head dbcc61a (origin/fix/mf-audit-profile-json): aitools-json.pl:28-40 and :176-192 ('an existing key ignoring case is an error, exit 2: set: '<seg>' differs only in case from existing key'), aitools-json.ps1:47-49 and :104-133 ('Segments match case-sensitively ... A new segment that equals an existing key ignoring case is refused'; Assert-JNoCaseTwin). grep -i 'case-insens|case twin|exact-match|key case' in reference/user-repo.md, reference/script-standards-detail.md and reference/cross-platform-detail.md: no hits. On origin/main 8a9dcb5 (the PR is still open): the rule is not only undocumented but also differs between the engines: PowerShell Set-JValue looks up segments case-insensitively while perl matches exactly (S3-MF-Audit A-9). PR #108 aligns them; this entry is the missing spec either way.
expected: No spec exists for: key-case behaviour of profile.json and the other JSON files the engines write. reference/user-repo.md is the profile.json spec; .claude/rules/documentation-standards.md 'one authoritative location per fact'.
impact: A user or tool that writes `ToolExceptions` or `Profiles` by hand gets a refusal (exit 2) or an ignored key with no documented reason; the next engine change (or a new writer in node or python) can pick a different rule, and bash and PowerShell diverge again (the S3-MF-Audit A-9 class).
discoveryContext: Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22, from the final marker batch relayed by S3-M3Finish. Marker I-5 from PR #108 (S3-MF-Fix6). Verified on dbcc61a with git show of both engine headers and grep of the three references. Audited #1-#165: #150 (number formatting differs) is the sibling engine-parity entry.
suggestedResolution: Add a 'Keys' paragraph to reference/user-repo.md (protected): keys are case-sensitive; a write that would create a key differing only in case from an existing one is refused (exit 2) in both engines; profile-key lookups that ignore case are done explicitly by the resolver. Point both engine headers at it.

title: The bash and PowerShell resolvers compare profile.json `version` differently: PowerShell accepts 2.0 and 20E-1 as version 2, bash rejects them as 'not v2', and no spec says how version is compared
observation: On PR #114 head f8e8fc0 (origin/fix/mf-audit-config): bash compares the raw JSON text, `if [ "$v" != "2" ]` (aitools-profile.sh:645, :1264, :1469); PowerShell compares `Get-JText` of the parsed value, `-ne "2"` (aitools-profile.ps1:514, :1120, :1298), and a Double 2.0 prints as 2. S3-MF-Incidents probe (scratch probe-final.sh, isolated HOME, the PR #114 scripts): version 2.0 and 20E-1 give bash 'profile.json is not v2' and PowerShell 'no profile matches this machine' (treated as v2); 2 and "2" are v2 in both. On origin/main 8a9dcb5 (the PR is still open): bash aitools-profile.sh:636, :1253, :1458 and PowerShell aitools-profile.ps1:513, :1093, :1271 compare the same way. The PR #102 reviewer reproduced the difference at engine level with an independent probe.
expected: .claude/rules/cross-platform.md 'Platform targeting principle' (paired scripts behave the same). No spec exists for: the allowed JSON encodings of profile.json `version` (integer only, or any numeric 2).
impact: A profile.json whose version a tool wrote as 2.0 resolves on Windows and fails on macOS/Linux, so the same dotprofile works on one machine and not the other.
discoveryContext: Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22, from the final marker batch relayed by S3-M3Finish. Marker from PR #114 (S3-MF-Fix3, probe at .claude/worktrees/mf-fix3/.scratch/session-mffix3/probe-version.sh). Re-run by S3-MF-Incidents on f8e8fc0 with its own probe (same result). Audited #1-#167: #150 (number formatting) is related.
suggestedResolution: State in reference/user-repo.md (protected) that `version` is the JSON integer 2, and make both resolvers accept exactly that (PowerShell: check the raw token or the type is an integer), or both accept any numeric value equal to 2. Add 2.0 / 20E-1 / "2" cases to tests/profile/test-profile.sh for both engines.

title: The Windows PowerShell profile function `function aitools { & aitools.ps1 @args }` passes `--alias <name>` through as a plain string, so `aitools user init --alias` (P-Q12) does not register the alias from a Windows shell
observation: scripts/aitools-install.ps1:530 (PR #116 head 1605d6e) writes the profile function `function aitools { & "`$HOME\.local\bin\aitools.ps1" @args }`. aitools.ps1:398-401 relies on pwsh binding `--alias` to -Alias 'under pwsh -File'. In-process `&` does not: S3-MF-Incidents probe (scratch probe-alias.ps1, pwsh 7 on macOS) with a script declaring [string]$Alias and ValueFromRemainingArguments: `aitools user init --alias box` through the wrapper (and a direct `&` call) left `--alias,box` in the remaining arguments; only `-Alias box` bound. The PR #116 reviewer (review B) reported the same; it predates PRs #103-#116. On origin/main 8a9dcb5 (the PR is still open): the same profile function is at aitools-install.ps1:511. The PR #102 reviewer confirmed option A: only `pwsh -File` binds `--alias`.
expected: Commander decision 1 / P-Q12 (S3-M3Lead plan section 2): `aitools user init --alias <new>` registers this machine's profile; .claude/rules/cross-platform.md (bash and PS1 entry points give the same result).
impact: On Windows, the documented `aitools user init --alias <name>` from a PowerShell prompt silently ignores the alias: user init falls back to the menu on a terminal or an ERROR without one, while the same command works in bash.
discoveryContext: Filed by S3-MF-Incidents (mission M3-FINISH item 9, Session Commander 10cf255a-c), 2026-10-22, from the final marker batch relayed by S3-M3Finish. Marker from PR #116 reviewer B. Verified: aitools-install.ps1:530 and aitools.ps1:5-21, :398-401 on 1605d6e; probe run on macOS only (the real aitools.ps1 exits at its OS guard there, so a stand-in script with the same parameter shape was used). Not run on Windows. Audited #1-#169: no match (#75 is the older alias-persistence gap).
suggestedResolution: Options: (A) the profile function invokes `pwsh -NoProfile -File aitools.ps1 @args` (binding then matches the -File path, at the cost of a child process); (B) aitools.ps1 maps `--alias <v>` (and other `--long` forms) out of $Remaining itself; (C) document `-Alias` for Windows. B keeps one process and fixes every caller; add a test that calls through the profile function.
